summary: Case-maps one character to uppercase. For 8-bit values (charCode <= 0xFF) uses the CRT ctype flag byte byte_8D47E1 (bit 0x20 = lowercase) and the precomputed uppercase table byte_8D46E0. For larger values the input is reassembled into a wide codepoint and, when byte_8D47E1 marks a lead byte (bit 0x4), locale-aware sub_591FA1 performs the mapping using locale handles dword_8D48E4 and dword_8D46BC. When no mapping applies the input is returned unchanged.

operations.description: charCode <= 0xFF selects the single-byte fast path; larger values take the multibyte/locale path.
Ctype flag check: bit 0x20 of byte_8D47E1[charCode] set means the 8-bit character is lowercase and can be uppercased via the table.
Return byte_8D46E0[charCode], the precomputed uppercase mapping from the 8-bit table.

Reassemble the multibyte input into a 16-bit wide codepoint: BYTE2(charCode) = BYTE1(charCode) and HIBYTE(charCode) = low byte. The later lead-byte test reads byte_8D47E1 from the unmodified original value (BYTE1(v1)), not the reassembled one.
Ctype lead-byte check: bit 0x4 of byte_8D47E1[BYTE1(v1)] (second byte of the unmodified input) must be set, and sub_591FA1 must return non-zero, for the mapped result to be used.
Call sub_591FA1 with locale handle dword_8D48E4, flag 0x200u, the reassembled 2-byte codepoint, destination buffer DestStr, and dword_8D46BC as a later argument; returns a success flag.
On locale-mapping success, compose the uppercased 16-bit result from DestStr bytes: DestStr[1] + (DestStr[0] << 8).
Default path: return charCode unchanged when no uppercase mapping applies.

unresolved: Meaning of the 0x200u flag passed to sub_591FA1 is unknown.
Role of dword_8D46BC as a later argument to sub_591FA1 (locale vs LANGID) is unconfirmed.
Exact encoding produced by the byte reassembly (MBCS lead+trail into a 16-bit codepoint) is inferred, not independently verified.
Distinction between locale handles dword_8D48E4 and dword_8D46BC is unconfirmed.
